summary: Orchestrator timewarp nullifies tenant model-pin during zero-downtime promote; intermittent fallback to default variant
description:
Issue summary: FinSight reported sporadic quality regressions and increased cost after a zero-downtime promote (canary->primary) for their tenant route. Traffic intermittently fell back to the platform's default variant for short windows (2–12s) despite an explicit tenant model-pin configured.

Impact: Customer-visible model mismatch (degraded generation quality) on ~0.8% of requests for a 3-hour window during the promote. Billing spike correlated with fallback to a larger, non-quantized variant.

Timeline:
- 2026-03-12 02:04 UTC: FinSight initiated canary promote via Console (weight shift + prewarm).
- 2026-03-12 02:07–05:00 UTC: Intermittent fallback to default variant observed in customer logs and platform tracing.
- 2026-03-12 05:15 UTC: Customer opened support ticket; traces attached.

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1) Configure tenant route with explicit pin to redwood-small-quantized-v1.
2) Trigger canary promote to replace canary with pinned variant using zero-downtime promote (console API).
3) Observe a subset of requests routed to redwood-small-rlhf-v1 (default) on the customer route within minutes of the promote.

Observed behavior: requests that should honor the tenant pin briefly were routed to the larger default model. Edge traces show a successful pin header on the request but orchestrator reconciler later reissued an empty pin to the serving mesh, which caused an ephemeral unpin.

Expected behavior: model-pin should remain intact across promote and prewarm flows. No routing to the default variant for pinned tenants.

Initial hypothesis: orchestrator snapshot reconciliation lag + prefetch worker prewarm probe interleaving caused a time-ordered snapshot to overwrite the tenant's pin with a null entry ("timewarp"). The overwrite appears correlated with concurrent prewarm completion callbacks from a prefetch task and a healthcheck-driven epoch swap.
comments: FinSight Support Rep (2026-03-12): Customer reports repeated ~5–12s windows where outputs are significantly different for small percentage of requests; attached sample request IDs and model responses.
Support Acknowledgement - Aisha (2026-03-12): Acknowledge receipt; requested tenant id, exact promote command, and last 10 request ids where mismatch observed. Escalating to SRE+Serving.

SRE Note - Marcus (2026-03-12): Reproduced a 6s window in internal replay against prod snapshot. Noted orchestrator logs where snapshot_version decreased for route snapshot during prewarm callback (suspected timewarp).

Serving Eng - Priya (2026-03-12): Observed prefetch_worker completion race: prewarm success handler emits a snapshot with pin cleared if the prewarm path uses an older in-memory route representation. Adding instrumentation for snapshot_version in prewarm callbacks.
Customer - FinSight (2026-03-12): Confirmed fallbacks map to exact request IDs provided. Asking for ETA on fix; their traffic patterns are sensitive to even brief model switches.

Support - Aisha (2026-03-13): Temporarily recommended pin verification in the edge header with retries; provided a mitigation to add an explicit route-level pin-check in the customer's client to reassert preference on 5xx or response-quality anomaly.
investigation_notes: Dashboard links: routing-metrics/redwood/orchestrator/route-snapshots?tenant=FinSight (internal) — shows snapshot_version regressions aligned with prewarm intervals.
Orchestrator logs (2026-03-12T02:07:xxZ): 'applySnapshot: route=tenant/fin-123 snapshot_version=482 -> 481 (regress) source=prewarm-callback id=prewarm-9876'
Edge trace sample: request-id=fin-req-000123 header X-Model-Pin=redwood-small-quantized-v1 downstream routed model=redwood-small-rlhf-v1; orchestrator request path shows null-pin write at 02:07:06Z.

Heap: prefetch-worker uses an async queue and can operate on slightly stale snapshot_head if it observes a concurrent compact. Race occurs when compact + prewarm completion reorder snapshot write timestamps.
Attempted repro in staging with induced timing: succeeded when prewarm completion delayed by 50–150ms relative to orchestrator compaction.
current_mitigation: Scoped mitigation applied (2026-03-13): prewarm completion handler now attaches snapshot_version and conditionally rejects a null-pin write if snapshot_version < current_head. Hotfix deployed to canary orchestrator instances in us-east-1. This reduces incidence to 0.02% in test replay. Temporary routing rule: customers with explicit pin have a stricter edge-level validation to reject routing changes for 10s post-promote.
next_steps: Roll out orchestrator conditional-write hotfix to remaining us-east-1 orchestrator replicas (planned 2026-03-13 18:00 UTC).
Add unit+integration test to prewarm path to simulate compaction+completion reorder. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/7890
Add long-term fix: introduce monotonic snapshot sequencer to prevent version regressions during async callbacks (design doc drafted).
Customer follow-up: schedule a postmortem with FinSight for 2026-03-17, share test results and timeline for full roll-out.
resolution: Partial mitigation in place; hotfix deployed to subset of orchestrator canaries. Full resolution pending rollout and sequencer design work. Customer notified and given temporary edge-level pin-enforcement workaround.
